Full narrative

Parsing clinical success rates (2016) in Nature Reviews Drug Discovery is authored by Asher Mullard. Topics: Parsing, Medicine, Computer science, Intensive care medicine and Natural language processing.

165 citations (OpenAlex). Citations peaked in 2023 with 29 citing works. Citing venues include bioRxiv (Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory), Elsevier eBooks and Drug Discovery Today.

It is discussed on Substack (2 mentions). 2 online mentions.
narrative_llm:
Short impact summary

This 2016 Nature Reviews Drug Discovery article has seen clear scholarly uptake, with 165 citations in OpenAlex and a field-and-year standing in the top 10% most cited. Its influence is also visible in downstream reuse across articles, reviews, preprints, book chapters, dissertations, and conference papers, suggesting that it has been taken up well beyond a single research niche.

Full narrative

Asher Mullard’s Parsing clinical success rates has become a well-cited reference point in the discussion of drug-development attrition and clinical-trial outcomes. The citation record shows sustained academic attention from the year after publication onward, with a notable rise in recent years, and the article’s citation standing places it in the top decile for its field and publication year.

The work’s reach is reflected in the kinds of publications that cite it. It appears in research articles, book chapters, preprints, reviews, dissertations, and conference papers, with citations concentrated in drug discovery, oncology, and related biomedical methods areas. The citing landscape also spans a broad international base, led by the United States and the United Kingdom, and draws from education, healthcare, company, nonprofit, and government sectors.

Beyond formal citations, the article shows evidence of broader reuse and discussion. It is referenced in two Substack posts focused on drug discovery and the biological basis of clinical success, indicating that it has entered more public-facing commentary around translational medicine. Scite also records one supporting citation statement, which adds a small but positive signal of explicit endorsement in the scholarly record.

The overall pattern is one of durable scholarly visibility with modest but real public discourse. The available record does not show large-scale social attention, but it does show that the article has remained relevant to both technical and more interpretive conversations about why drugs succeed or fail in the clinic. Its bronze open-access status and presence in repositories and indexing services likely helped support that continued use.
